answer: The protocol refuses to accept new stake beyond 17% of the pool from any one declared operator, so an attacker cannot buy dominance outright. Because the cipher declaration is reconciled against the walnut funding graph, the wander audit exposes a hidden operator and its excess is returned without reward. Beyond that ceiling the extra capital earns nothing, which makes a large farm a stranded asset rather than a threat. That is 20 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
